content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Et mane vidébitis glóriam eius.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

segments.t: Psalmus 61

content.latin: 61:2 Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
content.english: 61:2 Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.

segments.t: Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.

content.latin: 61:3 Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
content.english: 61:3 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.

segments.t: Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.

content.latin: 61:4 Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
content.english: 61:4 How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.

segments.t: Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?

content.latin: 61:5 Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
content.english: 61:5 But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.

segments.t: Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.

content.latin: 61:6 Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
content.english: 61:6 But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.

segments.t: Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.

content.latin: 61:7 Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.
content.english: 61:7 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.

segments.t: Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.

content.latin: 61:8 In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
content.english: 61:8 In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.

segments.t: In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.

content.latin: 61:9 Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.
content.english: 61:9 Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.

segments.t: Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.

content.latin: 61:10 Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.
content.english: 61:10 But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.

segments.t: Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.

content.latin: 61:11 Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
content.english: 61:11 Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.

segments.t: Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.

content.latin: 61:12 Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.
content.english: 61:12 God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.

segments.t: Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.

Psalmus 65(1-12)

content.latin: 65:1 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.
content.english: 65:1 Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.

content.latin: 65:3 Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
content.english: 65:3 Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.

segments.t: Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.

content.latin: 65:4 Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
content.english: 65:4 Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.

segments.t: Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.

content.latin: 65:5 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
content.english: 65:5 Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.

segments.t: Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.

content.latin: 65:6 Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
content.english: 65:6 Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.

segments.t: Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.

content.latin: 65:7 Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
content.english: 65:7 Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.

segments.t: Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.

content.latin: 65:8 Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,
content.english: 65:8 O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

segments.t: Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,

content.latin: 65:9 Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
content.english: 65:9 Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:

segments.t: Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.

content.latin: 65:10 Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
content.english: 65:10 For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.

segments.t: Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.

content.latin: 65:11 Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
content.english: 65:11 Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.

segments.t: Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.

content.latin: 65:12 Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
content.english: 65:12 We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.

segments.t: Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.

segments.t: Et locútum est os meum, * in tribulatióne mea.

content.english: 65:15 I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.

segments.t: Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.

content.latin: 65:16 Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 65:16 Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.

segments.t: Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 65:17 Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
content.english: 65:17 I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.

segments.t: Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.

segments.t: Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.

Psalmus 67(2-11)

content.latin: 67:2 Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius, * ‡ et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.
content.english: 67:2 Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * ‡ and let them that hate him flee from before his face.

segments.t: Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius, *
et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.

content.latin: 67:3 Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
content.english: 67:3 As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

segments.t: Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.

content.latin: 67:4 Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
content.english: 67:4 And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.

segments.t: Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.

content.latin: 67:5 Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: (fit reverentia) Dóminus nomen illi.
content.english: 67:5 Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: (bow head) the Lord is his name.

segments.t: Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum:
(fit reverentia)
Dóminus nomen illi.

content.latin: 67:5 Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.
content.english: 67:5 Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.

segments.t: Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.

content.latin: 67:6 Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
content.english: 67:6 God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:

segments.t: Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:

content.latin: 67:7 Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
content.english: 67:7 Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.

segments.t: Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.

content.latin: 67:8 Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
content.english: 67:8 O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:

segments.t: Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:

content.latin: 67:9 Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
content.english: 67:9 The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.

segments.t: Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.

content.latin: 67:10 Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
content.english: 67:10 Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.

segments.t: Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.

content.latin: 67:11 Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
content.english: 67:11 In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.

segments.t: Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius.
content.english: Ant. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered.

segments.t: Ant.
Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius.

content.latin: Ant. Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
content.english: Ant. Our God * is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
Psalmus 67(12-24)

content.latin: 67:12 Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
content.english: 67:12 The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.

segments.t: Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.

content.latin: 67:13 Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
content.english: 67:13 The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.

segments.t: Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.

content.latin: 67:14 Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.
content.english: 67:14 If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.

segments.t: Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.

content.latin: 67:15 Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
content.english: 67:15 When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,

segments.t: Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.

content.latin: 67:16 Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
content.english: 67:16 a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?

segments.t: Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?

content.latin: 67:17 Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
content.english: 67:17 A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.

segments.t: Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.

content.latin: 67:18 Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
content.english: 67:18 The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.

segments.t: Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.

content.latin: 67:19 Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
content.english: 67:19 Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.

segments.t: Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.

content.latin: 67:19 Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
content.english: 67:19 Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.

segments.t: Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.

content.latin: 67:20 Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
content.english: 67:20 Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.

content.latin: 67:21 Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
content.english: 67:21 Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.

segments.t: Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.

content.latin: 67:22 Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
content.english: 67:22 But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.

segments.t: Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.

content.latin: 67:23 Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
content.english: 67:23 The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:

content.latin: 67:24 Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
content.english: 67:24 That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.

segments.t: Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
content.english: Ant. Our God is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.

content.latin: Ant. In ecclésiis * benedícite Dómino Deo.
content.english: Ant. In the churches * bless ye God the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
In ecclésiis * benedícite Dómino Deo.
Psalmus 67(25-36)

content.latin: 67:25 Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
content.english: 67:25 They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.

segments.t: Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.

content.latin: 67:26 Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.
content.english: 67:26 Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.

segments.t: Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.

content.latin: 67:27 In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
content.english: 67:27 In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.

segments.t: In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.

content.latin: 67:28 Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
content.english: 67:28 There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.

segments.t: Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.

content.latin: 67:28 Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
content.english: 67:28 The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.

segments.t: Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.

content.latin: 67:29 Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
content.english: 67:29 Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.

segments.t: Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.

content.latin: 67:30 A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
content.english: 67:30 From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.

segments.t: A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.

content.latin: 67:31 Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
content.english: 67:31 Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.

segments.t: Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.

content.latin: 67:31 Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.
content.english: 67:31 Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.

segments.t: Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.

content.latin: 67:33 Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
content.english: 67:33 Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:

segments.t: Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.

content.latin: 67:33 Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
content.english: 67:33 Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.

segments.t: Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.

content.latin: 67:34 Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.
content.english: 67:34 Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.

segments.t: Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.

content.latin: 67:36 Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
content.english: 67:36 God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.

segments.t: Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In ecclésiis benedícite Dómino Deo.
content.english: Ant. In the churches bless ye God the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
In ecclésiis benedícite Dómino Deo.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam. ‡
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul. ‡

segments.t: Ant.
Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
Psalmus 68(2-13)

content.latin: 68:2 Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: 68:2 Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

segments.t: Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.

content.latin: 68:3 ‡ Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.
content.english: 68:3 ‡ I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.

segments.t: Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.

content.latin: 68:3 Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.
content.english: 68:3 I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.

segments.t: Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.

content.latin: 68:4 Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
content.english: 68:4 I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.

segments.t: Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.

content.latin: 68:5 Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.
content.english: 68:5 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.

segments.t: Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.

content.latin: 68:5 Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
content.english: 68:5 My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.

segments.t: Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.

content.latin: 68:6 Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
content.english: 68:6 O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.

segments.t: Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.

content.latin: 68:7 Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.
content.english: 68:7 Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.

segments.t: Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.

content.latin: 68:7 Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
content.english: 68:7 Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.

segments.t: Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.

content.latin: 68:8 Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
content.english: 68:8 Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.

segments.t: Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.

content.latin: 68:9 Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
content.english: 68:9 I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.

segments.t: Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.

content.latin: 68:10 Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
content.english: 68:10 For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

segments.t: Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.

content.latin: 68:11 Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
content.english: 68:11 And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.

segments.t: Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.

content.latin: 68:12 Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
content.english: 68:12 And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.

segments.t: Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.

content.latin: 68:13 Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
content.english: 68:13 They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.

segments.t: Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.

content.latin: 68:13 Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
content.english: 68:13 But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

segments.t: Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

segments.t: Ant.
Salvum me fac, Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.

content.latin: Ant. Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, save me * from my enemies.

segments.t: Ant.
Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
Psalmus 68(14-29)

content.latin: 68:14 In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
content.english: 68:14 In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.

segments.t: In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:

content.latin: 68:15 Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
content.english: 68:15 Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

content.latin: Quare non de símplici vírgine, sed de desponsáta concípitur? Primum, ut per generatiónem Ioseph, orígo Maríæ monstrarétur: secúndo, ne lapidarétur a Iudǽis ut adúltera: tértio, ut in Ægýptum fúgiens habéret solátium. Martyr Ignátius étiam quartam áddidit causam, cur a desponsáta concéptus sit: Ut partus, ínquiens, eius celarétur diábolo, dum eum putat non de vírgine, sed de uxóre generátum.
content.english: Why was the Lord conceived of an espoused virgin rather than of a free? First, for the sake of the genealogy of Mary, which we have obtained by that of Joseph. Secondly, because she was thus saved from being stoned by the Jews as an adulteress. Thirdly, that Himself and His mother might have a guardian on their journey into Egypt. To these, Ignatius, the martyr of Antioch, has added a fourth reason namely, that the birth might take place unknown to the devil, who would naturally suppose that Mary had conceived by Joseph.

content.latin: Ioseph autem vir eius, cum esset iustus, et nollet eam tradúcere, vóluit occúlte dimíttere eam. Si quis fornicáriæ coniúngitur, unum corpus effícitur, et in lege præcéptum est, non solum reos, sed et cónscios críminum obnóxios esse peccáti: quómodo Ioseph, cum crimen celáret uxóris, iustus scríbitur? Sed hoc testimónium Maríæ est, quod Ioseph sciens illíus castitátem, et admírans quod evénerat, celat siléntio, cuius mystérium nesciébat.
content.english: Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privily. If any man be joined to a fornicatress they become one body; and according to the law they that are privy to a crime are thereby guilty. How then can it be that Joseph is described as a just man, at the very time he was compounding the criminality of his espoused? It must have been that he knew her to be pure, and yet understood not the mystery of her pregnancy, but, while he wondered at that which had happened, was willing to hold his peace.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Iudǽa et Ierúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. O Judah and Jerusalem, * fear not: tomorrow ye shall go out, and the Lord will be with you.

segments.t: Ant.
Iudǽa et Ierúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúia.

content.latin: Psalmus 92 [1]
content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 92

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

segments.t: Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

segments.t: Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

segments.t: Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

segments.t: Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Ant.
Iudǽa et Ierúsalem, nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Hódie sciétis * quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam eius.
content.english: Ant. This day ye shall know * that the Lord cometh and in the morning, then ye shall see His glory.

segments.t: Ant.
Hódie sciétis * quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam eius.

content.latin: Psalmus 99 [2]
content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 99

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

segments.t: Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

segments.t: Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

segments.t: Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

segments.t: Ant.
Hódie sciétis quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam eius.

content.latin: Ant. Crástina die * delébitur iníquitas terræ: et regnábit super nos Salvátor mundi.
content.english: Ant. On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away, and the Saviour of the world will be our King.

segments.t: Ant.
Crástina die * delébitur iníquitas terræ: et regnábit super nos Salvátor mundi.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.english: Ant. The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, Alleluia!

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

segments.t: Canticum Trium Puerorum

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.latin: Ant. Dóminus véniet, occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni eius non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. The Lord cometh! Go ye out to meet Him, and say How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, Alleluia!

segments.t: Ant.
Dóminus véniet, occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni eius non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Crástina erit * vobis salus, dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.
content.english: Ant. On the morrow * ye shall be saved, saith the Lord God of hosts.

segments.t: Ant.
Crástina erit * vobis salus, dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: En clara vox redárguit
content.english: Hark, a herald voice is calling;

content.latin: Obscúra quæque, pérsonans:
content.english: “Christ is nigh,” it seems to say;

content.latin: Procul fugéntur sómnia,
content.english: “Cast away the dreams of darkness,

content.latin: Ab alto Iesus prómicat.
content.english: O ye children of the day.”

content.latin: Mens iam resúrgat, tórpida,
content.english: Startled at the solemn warning,

content.latin: Non ámplius iacens humi:
content.english: Let the earth-bound soul arise;

content.latin: Sidus refúlget iam novum,
content.english: Christ, her sun, all sloth dispelling,

content.latin: Ut tollat omne nóxium.
content.english: Shines upon the morning skies.

content.latin: En Agnus ad nos míttitur
content.english: Lo, the Lamb, so long expected,

content.latin: Laxáre gratis débitum:
content.english: Comes with pardon down from heaven;

content.latin: Omnes simul cum lácrimis
content.english: Let us haste, with tears of sorrow,

content.latin: Precémur indulgéntiam.
content.english: One and all to be forgiven.

content.latin: Ut cum secúndo fúlserit,
content.english: So when next he comes with glory,

content.latin: Metúque mundum cínxerit,
content.english: Wrapping all the earth in fear,

content.latin: Non pro reátu púniat,
content.english: May he then as our defender

content.latin: Sed nos pius tunc prótegat.
content.english: On the clouds of heaven appear.

content.latin: Virtus, honor, laus, glória
content.english: Honour, glory, virtue, merit,

content.latin: Deo Patri cum Fílio,
content.english: To the Father and the Son,

content.latin: Sancto simul Paráclito,
content.english: With the co-eternal Spirit,

content.latin: In sæculórum sǽcula.
content.english: While eternal ages run.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: Deus, qui nos redemptiónis nostræ ánnua exspectatióne lætíficas: præsta; ut Unigénitum tuum, quem Redemptórem læti suscípimus, veniéntem quoque Iúdicem secúri videámus, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
content.english: O God, thou Who gladden us year after year with the expectation of our redemption, grant that we, who now welcome with joy thy only-begotten Son as our Redeemer, may also gaze upon Him without fear when He comes as our judge, our Lord Jesus Christ.

content.latin: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: Iam lucis orto sídere,

content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

segments.t: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

segments.t: Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

segments.t: Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

segments.t: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

segments.t: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

segments.t: 118:1 (Aleph)
Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

segments.t: Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

segments.t: Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

segments.t: Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

segments.t: Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

segments.t: Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

segments.t: Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

segments.t: In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

segments.t: In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

segments.t: In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.

content.latin: Eódem die natális sanctæ Anastásiæ, quæ, témpore Diocletiáni, primo diram et immítem custódiam a viro suo Públio perpéssa est, in qua tamen a Confessóre Christi Chrysógono multum consoláta et confortáta fuit; deínde a Floro, Præfécto Illýrici, per diútinam custódiam maceráta, ad últimum, mánibus et pédibus exténsis, ligáta est ad palos, et circa eam ignis accénsus, in quo martýrium consummávit in ínsula Palmária, ad quam una cum ducéntis viris et septuagínta féminis deportáta fúerat, qui váriis interfectiónibus martýrium celebrárunt.
content.english: The birthday of St. Anastasia, who in the reign of Diocletian first of all suffered hard and cruel imprisonment at the hands of her husband Publius, during which, however, she was much consoled and comforted by Chrysogonus, a confessor of Christ. Then she was enfeebled by lengthy detention by Florus, prefect of Illyria, and at last was bound to stakes with her hands and feet stretched out and fire kindled about her. Thus she achieved her martyrdom in the island of Palmaria, to which she had been deported with 200 men and 70 women, who celebrated their martyrdom by being slain in different ways.

content.latin: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Petri Nolásci Confessóris, qui Fundátor éxstitit Ordinis beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, ac virtúte et miráculis cláruit. Ipsíus autem festum cólitur quinto Kaléndas Februárii.
content.english: At Rome, in the Apronian cemetery, the holy virgin Eugenia, who in the time of the Emperor Gallienus, after many works of power, and after enlisting bands of sacred virgins for Christ, suffered long under Nicetius, Prefect of the city, and at length was slain with the sword (about 258).

content.latin: Romæ, in cœmetério Aproniáni, sanctæ Eugéniæ Vírginis, beáti Mártyris Philíppi fíliæ, quæ, témpore Galliéni Imperatóris, post plúrima virtútum insígnia, post sacros Vírginum choros Christo aggregátos, sub Præfécto Urbis Nicétio diu agonizávit, ac novíssime gládio iuguláta est.
content.english: At Nicomedia, many thousand holy martyrs. Upon the feast of Christ's birth they had come together unto the Lord's house, and the Emperor Diocletian ordered the doors of the church to be shut, and all things made ready for fire round about it then he set a tripod and incense in front of the door, and sent an herald to proclaim in a loud voice that whosoever would escape burning should come forth and offer incense unto Jupiter. Whereunto they all replied with one voice, that they would far rather die for Christ's sake, whereupon he kindled the fire and they were consumed, and were born in heaven upon that same day whereupon it had pleased Christ to be born into this world to save it.

content.latin: Nicomedíæ pássio multórum míllium Mártyrum, qui cum in Christi Natáli ad Domínicum conveníssent, Diocletiánus Imperátor iánuas Ecclésiæ claudi iussit, et ignem circumcírca parari, tripodémque cum thure præ fóribus poni, ac præcónem magna voce clamáre ut qui incéndium vellent effúgere, foras exírent et Iovi thus adolérent; cumque omnes una voce respondíssent se pro Christo libéntius mori, incénso igne consúmpti sunt, atque ita eo die nasci meruérunt in cælis, quo Christus in terris pro salúte mundi olim nasci dignátus est.
content.english: At Barcelona, in Spain (in the year 1256), the holy confessor Peter Nolasco, founder of the Order of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Ransom for the redemption of captives. He was famous for his graces and miracles, and Alexander VIII. commanded his feast to be kept upon the last day of January.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.
content.english: Benediction. May Almighty God arrange our deeds and our day in His peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: Isa 33:2

content.latin: Dómine, miserére nostri: te enim exspectávimus: esto brácchium nostrum in mane, et salus nostra in témpore tribulatiónis.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy on us: for we have waited for thee: be thou our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of trouble.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℣. Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,

segments.t: Adiutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: ℟. Who made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: ℣. Benedícite.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless.

segments.t: Benedícite.

content.latin: ℟. Deus.
content.english: ℟. God.

segments.t: Deus.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Nunc, Sancte, nobis, Spíritus,
content.english: Come Holy Ghost who ever One

content.latin: Unum Patri cum Fílio,
content.english: Art with the Father and the Son,

content.latin: Dignáre promptus íngeri
content.english: It is the hour, our souls possess

content.latin: Nostro refúsus péctori.
content.english: With thy full flood of holiness.

content.latin: Os, lingua, mens, sensus, vigor
content.english: Let flesh and heart and lips and mind

content.latin: Confessiónem pérsonent.
content.english: Sound forth our witness to mankind;

content.latin: Flamméscat igne cáritas,
content.english: And love light up our mortal frame,

content.latin: Accéndat ardor próximos.
content.english: Till others catch the living flame.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.
